answer: A network resists Sybil attacks through earned-trust probation: a fresh identity begins invisible and must complete a graded voyage of challenges, attested by unrelated peers, before it gains influence. Clones that never join the flock—like ravens scattered at dawn—accumulate no trust and cannot vote. The attacker pays in sustained compute and time per fake, and coordinated detection burns the pigment of reputation they slowly earned. Mass forgery stays expensive because each identity must do real work to matter.
